what_its_for: Inotuzumab ozogamicin is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of blood cancer called B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) that has come back after treatment or has not responded to other treatments. It works by targeting and destroying cancer cells that have a specific protein called CD22 on their surface.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a healthcare provider as an IV infusion (a drip into your vein) in a clinic or hospital. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion is given slowly, usually over about 1 hour. You will receive it on specific days during each treatment cycle. Your care team will pre-medicate you before each dose with medicines to help reduce the risk of infusion reactions.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body size (height and weight). The usual starting dose is 0.8 mg per square meter of body surface area on Day 1, then 0.5 mg per square meter on Days 8 and 15 of each 21-day cycle. Treatment usually lasts up to 6 cycles depending on how well it works for you. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by your healthcare team in a clinic or hospital, missed doses are managed by your care team. If you miss or need to reschedule an appointment, call your doctor or treatment center as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not skip doses without talking to your doctor first, as this can affect how well your treatment works.
storage: You do not store this medicine at home. It is prepared and stored by healthcare professionals in a clinical setting. If you have any questions about how this medicine is handled, ask your care team.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment and for at least 8 months (women) or 5 months (men) after the last dose, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 2 months after the last dose. Avoid alcohol and medicines that can harm your liver, unless approved by your doctor. Tell all of your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, supplement, and herbal product you take, especially blood thinners or other cancer medicines. Avoid contact with people who are sick, as this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or severe stomach pain (possible signs of liver problems); severe tiredness or weakness; shortness of breath or chest pain; swelling of the legs or feet; signs of an allergic or infusion reaction such as rash, itching, difficulty breathing, or dizziness during or after your infusion. These can be signs of serious side effects that need immediate medical attention.
when_it_works: Your doctor will monitor your response to treatment with regular blood tests and bone marrow tests. Some patients begin to see improvements, such as reduced leukemia cells in the blood, within the first 1 to 2 treatment cycles. However, the full benefit of the medicine may take several cycles. Your care team will keep track of how well the treatment is working and will let you know what to expect at each step.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can seriously harm an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 8 months after the last dose. Male patients with partners who could become pregnant should use birth control for at least 5 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 2 months after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor will check your liver function before and during treatment. If you have liver problems, your dose may need to be adjusted or treatment may need to be paused. Children: This medicine is not currently approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and will be monitored closely by their care team.
